discrepancies.title: OM yield 8.3% is on asking price, before 6.2% acquisition costs

sources.label: acquisition costs (DLD 4%, broker, trustee, mortgage registration)

discrepancies.why: A buyer pays AED 5,932,407 on top of the price. On price plus costs the same income gives 7.8%.

impact.basis: OM income on price plus acquisition costs, minus the stated yield

discrepancies.analyst_action: Compare deals on yield on total cost; ask the broker to restate the yield on that basis.

discrepancies.title: Area basis: the OM's AED 752/sq ft is on BUA without saying so; on NSA it is AED 976/sq ft

sources.label: OM price per sq ft (basis not stated)
price per sq ft NSA (rent-roll area)

discrepancies.why: Price per sq ft and opex per sq ft are only comparable on the same area basis. The screen uses the rent roll's unit areas (converted to sq ft) as NSA.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the title deed and affection plan areas; restate price per sq ft on NSA.

discrepancies.title: OM unit count or mix differs from the rent roll: OM 120 units vs rent roll 118; studio: OM 24 vs roll 20; 1br: OM 72 vs roll 74

sources.quote: 120 units: 24 x studio, 72 x 1 bedroom, 24 x 2 bedroom
sources.label: OM unit mix
rent roll unit count by type

discrepancies.why: The rent roll lists the units that exist and are leased; an OM mix that differs is often a developer brochure figure or includes merged / combined units.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the as-built unit schedule (DLD / affection plan) and reconcile unit numbers.

discrepancies.title: 54.8% of in-place rent expires between 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-29

sources.label: leases ending 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-29 (rent roll lease end dates)

discrepancies.why: A cluster of expiries means one leasing season sets most of the income, in a falling market. The mandate limit is 40.0% in any 3-month window of the 12 months from 2026-10-31.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the renewal status and notices on the expiring leases; consider a price holdback or rent guarantee.

notices.text: Tenants' security deposits of AED 391,800 transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
Cheque profile: 43% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 37% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 20% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.

rejected_model_findings.title: Headline rental income appears to include rent for vacant units

evidence.quote: Rental income as per the current rent roll. Yield calculated on the asking price.

rejected_model_findings.why: The OM presents AED 7,960,000 as rental income "as per the current rent roll" and does not say it is potential rent. The parsed rent roll (as of 2026-10-31) shows 5 vacant units and 1 notice-served unit, yet in-place rent and potential rent are both AED 7,958,500. That suggests the OM figure, and the 8.34% yield built on it, includes asking rent for vacant units. Contracted rent from let units would be lower, and so would the yield.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Ask the seller for the rent roll with contracted rent for let units only, showing asking rent for vacant units separately. Recompute gross and net yield on contracted rent. Also confirm how the 96% occupancy figure was derived and its date.
rejected_model_findings.rejected_because: contradicted by the rent roll: OM income AED 7,960,000 equals in-place rent AED 7,958,500 within 2%

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the deal misses the unlevered IRR and equity multiple targets at asking, and over half the rent expires in one three-month window.

Buy at AED 69.1m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That is 28% below asking [[uw.walk_away_vs_asking]] against an asking price of AED 95.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The assumption that most moves the walk-away price is the exit yield, at 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] either way, which shifts the price by AED 9.3m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and the returns rest on the firm's house view (reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Vireo Residences, Dubai Silicon Oasis. G+P+6, completed 2024 [[deal.completion_year]]. 118 units [[rr.unit_count]] on the rent roll (the OM says 120 [[om.unit_count]]). Freehold, single title.
- **Price:** AED 95.5m [[uw.price_aed]], which is AED 976 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on net sellable area. The OM's AED 752 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_bua]] is on built-up area.
- **Income:** In-place rent is AED 8.0m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. Occupancy is 96% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] by units and 95% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area. All leases are direct, with no master tenant, and tenants pay the chiller. 55% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of rent expires in one window.

## Returns
Unlevered, pre-tax:

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR | 4.3% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]], fails |
| Equity multiple | 1.20x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]], fails |
| Entry yield on price | 6.5% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 6.1% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]], passes |

Year-1 NOI is AED 6.2m [[uw.noi_year1]].

Levered, secondary: IRR 2.5% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]], equity multiple 1.13x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]], Year-1 DSCR 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM's headline yield is 8.3% [[om.yield_stated]], gross on asking price. On a buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 6.1% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]]. The gap against the OM figure is negative: the buyer's yield is lower by 2.2 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]].

## What would make it fail
- **Exit yield and rent.** With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, unlevered IRR is 1.7% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. Levered IRR is a loss of 1.6% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]] a year.
- **No grid case reaches the target.** The best case has market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter. Unlevered IRR there is 6.8% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], still under the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target.
- **Expiry cluster.** AED 4.4m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]] of rent expires between 31 January 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 29 April 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. The house view has market rents falling 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1, so renewals could reset lower.

## Discrepancies
All four are medium severity. Any lower-severity items are not discussed.
1. **Expiry concentration.** 55% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent expires in one window, against a mandate limit of 40% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]]. The screen relied on the rent roll. One leasing season would set most of the income.
2. **Yield before acquisition costs.** The OM's 8.3% [[om.yield_stated]] is on asking price, before acquisition costs of 6.2% [[uw.acquisition_costs_pct_of_price]], or AED 5.9m [[uw.acquisition_costs_aed]]. On price plus costs, the OM's own income gives 7.8% [[uw.om_yield.stated_income_on_total_cost]], which is 0.5 points [[disc.yield_excludes_acquisition_costs.impact_ratio]] lower. The screen used its own engine figures.
3. **Area basis.** The OM does not say its AED 752 per sq ft [[om.price_psf_stated]] is on built-up area of 127,060 sq ft [[deal.bua_sqft]]. On the rent roll's net area of 97,834 sq ft [[rr.area_sqft_total]] it is AED 976 per sq ft [[disc.area_basis_confusion.impact_value]]. The screen used the rent roll.
4. **Unit mix.** The OM shows 24 studios [[disc.unit_mix_mismatch.title]] and 72 one-bedroom units [[disc.unit_mix_mismatch.title]], against 20 studios [[rr.studio.units]] and 74 one-bedroom units [[rr.1br.units]] on the rent roll. The screen used the rent roll, which lists the units that exist and are leased.

## Checks before diligence
- Get renewal status and notices on the expiring leases. 1 [[rr.status.notice_served]] unit has already served notice. Consider a price holdback or rent guarantee.
- Ask the broker to restate yield on total cost.
- Get title deed and affection plan areas, and restate price per sq ft on net area.
- Get the as-built unit schedule and reconcile unit numbers.
- Credit tenants' security deposits of AED 392k [[uw.security_deposits_aed]] to the buyer at closing.
- Review the cheque profile. More cheques mean more collection risk.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search, including buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled unit by unit.
- Civil Defence and fire-safety certificates, and cladding compliance.

## Assumptions
The exit yield is 7.0% [[uw.exit_yield]] after 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion plus an age premium, over a hold of 5 [[uw.hold_years]] years. Market rent falls 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2. It then rises 2% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss is 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. The loan is 43% [[uw.ltv]] of value, under the 45% [[assume.max_ltv]] cap. It is sized at 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]] cover, at 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] interest, amortising over 15 [[assume.amortisation_years]] years. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
